- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices during sharp downward trends, particularly when true values dip below 65–70.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility: forecasts overshoot after price spikes, then fail to correct downward.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true mean.
- Fails to capture mean reversion in the final 5–10 days of forecast, often holding high values when true prices are declining.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of forecast, especially when true values are trending downward.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward momentum; often forecasts remain high until true values drop below 70.
- Overestimates prices in the middle of forecast horizon (days 10–20) when true values are typically lower.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of forecast, especially when true values are trending downward.
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then underestimates in the final 5–10 days.
